# `reduct.compass()` {#fn-reduct-compass}

W02 checked north-crossing magnetic readings against the supplied corrections before passing true bearings into a skyline analysis. [W02 results](w02-field-to-sky.qmd).

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-reduct-compass)

```{=html}
<p>Magnetic north differs from true north at the time and place of survey. Add the supplied
magnetic declination to each magnetic bearing, or calculate it from the survey
coordinates and date with mag.dec. Corrected bearings are rounded using the input
bearing representation. With an explicit altitude or a measured horizon, the corrected
bearing also enters the conversion to declination.
</p>
<p>Supply either a measurement date or a known magnetic declination.
If both are given, the supplied magnetic declination is used and the date is
retained in the output. Explicit altitude values take precedence over a
horizon profile. Otherwise, each measurement's corrected true azimuth is
used to retrieve its horizon altitude; the same altitude is reported and
used to calculate celestial declination. Supply one site and date for the whole
survey or one location row and/or date per bearing, in measurement order.
A supplied correction can likewise be shared or paired with each bearing.
</p>
```

[Source and date of the magnetic correction](fn-mag-dec.qmd).


<details><summary>Implementation arguments, return value and documented modes</summary>

```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>loc</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Location, either a <em>skyscapeR.horizon</em> or a vector
containing the latitude, longitude and elevation of location, in this order.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>mag.az</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Array of magnetic azimuth measurements.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>date</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Date of measurements as a string in the format: 'YYYY/MM/DD'.
Only necessary if <em>magdec</em> is not given. When omitted, the output
Date column contains missing values (NA).</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>magdec</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Magnetic declination, if known.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>alt</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Altitude, necessary for automatic declination calculation.
If missing and <em>loc</em> is a <em>skyscapeR.horizon</em> object then the altitude
will be automatically read from the horizon profile.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>name</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Names or labels to identify each measurement.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>ID</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>IDs or codes to identify each measurement.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>HWT.ID</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>HeyWhatsThat IDs relating to a previously generated
horizon profile for measurement.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>A data frame with one row per measurement, including location,
magnetic azimuth, date, magnetic declination and true azimuth. Altitude and
celestial declination are included when altitudes are supplied or a horizon
is available. Optional identification columns are retained.
</p>
```

</details>

**Implementation.** `R/data-reduction.R`.
